newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Southeast Asian wheat imports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Southeast Asian wheat imports seen rising.

text.p: Southeast Asian consumption of wheat and wheat-based products will rise sharply as the region's newly rich young diversify their choice of meals away from a simple diet of rice, an analyst said on Friday.

John Howard, vice-president for South Asia of U.S. Wheat Associates, told delegates at an Asia rice conference in Singapore the increasing urbanisation and income growth in the region will lead to an expanded market for wheat.
"They (young people) are less tied to traditional ways," Howard said. "When your buyers are under 20 years old, they can do it (change eating habits) in a heartbeat."

At least half of Indonesia's 200 million people are under 20 years of age. Some 52 percent of Vietnam's 73 million people and about 45 percent of Thailand's nearly 65 million people are also below 20.
At least 40 percent of 68 million people in the Philippines are also below 20 years.
By comparison, only 30 percent of the United States' 260 million people are below 20, Howard said.
Southeast Asian imports of wheat have surged to over nine million tonnes this year from three million tonnes in 1978, he added.
"We see a greater demand for flour-based products," Howard said. "It's cheaper to eat wheat. You can sell your rice and make more money."

Imports by Indonesia, the top importer of U.S. wheat in the region, will rise by five percent annually to the year 2000. Jakarta's wheat imports will probably reach 4.0 million tonnes in the 1996/97 (July 1/June 30) marketing year.
Philippine wheat imports for 1996/97 are expected to remain stable at around 2.0-2.2 million tonnes.
Indonesia is the eighth largest importer of wheat in the world. The Philippines ranks 11th.
